The business rules it holds belong in a domain layer: the 1-8 seat limit, refusing sales once an event has started, selling seats through Event.sell, building the ticket code, and admitting tickets through Ticket.admit. It talks to EventStore and TicketStore only by calling their methods (load, saveSeatsSold, add, markScanned, upcoming). It contains no SQL, connections, serialization formats, transport or framework code. The borderline part is that it rebuilds Event and Ticket entities from raw store rows (new Event(data.id, ...) and new Ticket(data.code, ...)) and spreads the ticket for storage ({ ...ticket }). These are light mapping steps that a repository could do instead. They don't amount to real persistence logic in the domain file, so I'm not counting them as a violation. The fact that the file imports from the persistence layer is an import-direction question, which is out of scope here.
